clue.text: Prince standing on his head, say, in lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the prince sits on top of the next piece, so he comes first

parts.note: Prince Caspian is the title hero of a Narnia novel by C. S. Lewis

indicators.note: say signals that the letter C is spoken and heard as a body of salt water

parts.note: the head of the prince's name is its first letter, C

explanation.surface: A prince doing a headstand in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' is the first letter of the prince's name, C, which when spoken sounds like SEA; 'standing on' places the prince above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian is the world's largest inland body of water, often classed as a lake despite its name.

clue.text: Corrupt gain is in 16, for example

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the following letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten gains finding their way into the national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A national flag such as the Stars and Stripes is an emblem, one kind of distinguishing badge.

clue.text: This is spinning plus a source of radiation

definitions.text: This is spinning plus a source of radiation

indicators.note: spinning means turning round and round, so the letters of the word plus are rearranged
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A description of a rotating star that sends out radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the R of radiation; the whole clue also describes the object, a rapidly rotating neutron star emitting beams.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapidly rotating neutron star emits regular pulses of radio waves, matching a spinning emitter.

clue.text: Marchers ignoring the odds — points of no return?

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Marching soldiers taking no chances, heading somewhere they cannot come back from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points of no return' is a tennis joke: a serve the opponent cannot hit back wins a point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve that the receiver fails to touch scores a point with no return made.

clue.text: Offended, in France, very old-fashioned duke

parts.note: in French very is tres and old-fashioned is passe, so the phrase is tres passe

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned French nobleman who has taken offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass in the biblical sense is to sin, to commit an offence against someone.

clue.text: A dubious character, this masked man in theatre?

explanation.surface: A shady figure who hides behind a mask on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, where the surgeon wears a mask, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth operator is a slick schemer; a surgeon performs operations in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Names last of three Europeans leaving Pacific island earlier

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the letter is taken out of the island name

parts.note: Celebes is the former name of the Indonesian island now called Sulawesi
E stands for European; the old island name has three of them and the last one goes

explanation.surface: Europeans departing from a Pacific island at an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities are big names; famous people are often called names in phrases like household names.

clue.text: What every solver thinks, initially, is the point of setting

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: A remark about what all crossword solvers believe the setter is aiming at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' looks like crossword setting, but it is the sun going down.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sets in the direction opposite sunrise, the compass point where setting happens.

clue.text: Presenter with top-notch Republican introducing new part of speech

indicators.note: introducing means bringing inside, so the following pieces go into the word for top-notch

parts.note: an ace is someone or something first-rate
a noun is one grammatical part of speech

explanation.surface: A first-rate politician bringing in a new grammatical term while broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who introduces programmes or reads the news is a presenter on radio or television.

clue.text: Man on board in calm sound

indicators.note: sound here means heard spoken, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: peace is a state of calm

explanation.surface: A man staying calm aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman or draughtsman is a playing token on the board.

clue.text: Ministers planting parts of it in the media

indicators.note: in places the second letter inside the word for the media as well
planting means setting into the ground, so the letters go inside the word for the media

parts.note: the press is a collective name for the news media
the first of the two letters of the word it, used as a separate part
the second of the two letters of the word it, planted separately

explanation.surface: Government ministers placing stories in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of IT are planted separately: I after PR and T after PRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergymen minister to a congregation, and a minister is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Most active 11, when last becomes first

indicators.note: the final letter of the referenced word is moved round to the front

parts.note: refers to the entry for clue 11 across, meaning ministers of religion

explanation.surface: The most energetic cleric, ordered so that the last shall be first.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction echoes the biblical saying that the last shall be first.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and lively; its superlative describes whoever is the liveliest.

clue.text: Device for removing bristles from jaw, nervously

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are found within the words jaw nervously

explanation.surface: Someone shaving their jaw anxiously with a razor.
explanation.walkthrough: Awns are the bristles on ears of barley; this machine knocks them off, not stubble from a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Awns are the stiff bristles on grain heads, and this machine strips them from threshed barley.

clue.text: Pure daughter is taken inside to be scolded

indicators.note: taken inside means placed within, so the word is goes into the other letters

parts.note: chaste means pure or virginal

explanation.surface: A virtuous daughter being brought indoors for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to rebuke or reprimand them severely.

clue.text: It's not repackaged in attractive form

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for attractive

parts.note: cute means pretty or attractive

indicators.note: repackaged means wrapped up again differently, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A product that has not been rewrapped in a pretty presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reads like a noun after 'attractive', but it is the verb meaning to make up; the apostrophe in It's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up or compose a whole is to form it, as members make up a committee.

clue.text: Refuses to accept right correction in records

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for records

parts.note: discs are gramophone records
an edit is a correction or revision

explanation.surface: Someone declining to accept a correct amendment in the official records.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to reject it or cause it to be disbelieved.

clue.text: Standard 7, such as 8, 20, 21 down, 22 down and 23 across or 3 and 18, together with 11, 12, or 22 across, possibly

parts.words: 7, such as 8, 20, 21 down, 22 down and 23 across or 3 and 18
parts.note: clue 7 means celebrities, and the listed entries are film celebrities or heavenly bodies, all examples of stars
together with means plus, so the word and

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement of the letters of the referenced entries

parts.note: these three entries all share the same seven letters, any one of them serving as the fodder

explanation.surface: A long list of cross-references describing a famous national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West, Burton, Streep, Peck and Garland are film stars; a pulsar and the Pleiades are stars in the sky. Each of 11, 12 and 22 across is an anagram of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag of the United States is a national standard, a banner flown as an emblem.

clue.text: Fighters sorry, oddly, about veteran

indicators.note: about means around, so the odd letters of sorry go round the word for veteran
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: an oldie is an old person or veteran

explanation.surface: Troops apologising around an old soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective noun for a body of soldiers, people who fight.

clue.text: Source of light at night as unorthodox sleep aid

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd way of helping someone fall asleep by night-light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleep aid' tempts towards a night-light; the source of light is a star cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sisters star cluster in Taurus shines in the night sky.

clue.text: Leader of army badly lamed, but proceeded on foot

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
badly signals that the letters of lamed but are put into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A commander whose troops were crippled but carried on marching.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambulate is to walk about, a formal word for moving on foot.

clue.text: Standing in stream to drink

indicators.note: standing in means placed within, so the word to sits inside the word for stream

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: Someone standing in a brook to have a drink of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Burton is a strong ale from Burton upon Trent, an English brewing town; the actor Richard Burton is the themed star.
explanation.definitionFit: Burton ale is a strong dark English beer named after its brewing town, so a drink.

clue.text: Shepherd and animal from herd

explanation.surface: A shepherd and a beast from his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd is to guide or direct; a young castrated bull is one beast in a herd of cattle.

clue.text: Stupidly pester top American player

indicators.note: stupidly means in a foolish or disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly bothering a leading US actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is a leading American actress, a player in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: To continue getting coverage in papers is terrible

indicators.note: the answer is covered by the surrounding words, sitting inside the run papers is terrible

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that ongoing press coverage is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere or keep going is to carry on despite difficulty.

clue.text: Nibble at food a lot

explanation.surface: Eating a small amount of something versus a large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds pick at grain with their beaks; a bushel-sized measure also stands for a large quantity.

clue.text: Newspaper's turn to secure literary anthology

indicators.note: turn means reverse direction, so the word for newspaper is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper
to land something is to secure or win it

explanation.surface: A newspaper taking its turn to obtain an anthology of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland in older literary usage is a collection of poems or ballads, a bouquet of verse.

clue.text: Medal held by Pentagon general

indicators.note: held by means contained in, so the letters are found inside the words Pentagon general

explanation.surface: A decoration kept by a US military chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration awarded for service.

clue.text: One's found in church or part of cathedral

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the numeral goes into the other letters

parts.note: one is represented by the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is in a church or in a section of a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel area where singers sit, east of the nave, is a named section of a cathedral.

clue.text: Take care of English prop most sensitive to pain

parts.note: to tend is to look after or take care of
a rest is a support or prop

explanation.surface: Caring for an English support that hurts at the slightest touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means sore and painful to the touch, and this is its superlative form.
